extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and implementing the Department of Education's final §106.44 requirements for how recipients must detect, report, respond to, prevent, and remedy sex discrimination in their education programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly and effectively when recipient has knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a)(1): a recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity must respond promptly and effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must end any sex discrimination that has occurred, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects. The nature of the response depends on the person's role, and the recipient must ensure all of its employees fulfill the duty to respond. This obligation is triggered when the recipient has 'knowledge' as defined elsewhere in §106.44 (e.g., information to a non-confidential employee). The Department clarified this is not strict liability for conduct that occurred before any employee had knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient must comply with §106.44(b)-(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a)(2): a recipient must comply with this section to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance requires taking the specific actions outlined in §106.44(b)-(k), which set forth steps both to ensure recipients have knowledge of possible sex discrimination and to respond appropriately when they do. This provision was added to avoid an open-ended obligation and to give specific instructions for required actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded knowledge standard — information to non-confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is deemed to have knowledge of sex-based discrimination and an obligation to respond when any non-confidential employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All non-confidential employees of elementary and secondary schools must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information. At other recipients, employees with responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising must notify the Title IX Coordinator. All other non-confidential employees at non-elementary/non-secondary recipients must either notify the Title IX Coordinator or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and information about how to make a complaint to any person who provides the employee with information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (see §106.44(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-confidential employee immediate duties
rubrics_metrics.description: When a non-confidential employee has information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, they must respond promptly and effectively by either notifying the Title IX Coordinator or providing the complainant with the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and information about how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty applies to Title IX Coordinators, contractors delegated Title IX responsibilities, and other non-confidential employees as specified; employees must follow the notification pathways required by §106.44(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge-required safeguard — not strict liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal to the knowledge expansion, the recipient 'with knowledge' must respond; the Department does not impose strict liability for sex discrimination that occurred before an employee became aware of the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(a) to clarify that obligations are triggered only when the recipient has knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination; if no employee (including Title IX Coordinator or delegated contractor) has such knowledge, the recipient cannot be expected to respond promptly and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective threshold for response — 'reasonably may constitute' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient need not have incontrovertible proof that conduct violates Title IX; if the conduct reasonably may be sex discrimination, the recipient must respond in accordance with §106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with prior guidance and case law (e.g., Doe v. Fairfax Cnty. Sch. Bd., Davis), an objectively plausible report that can be taken to allege sexual harassment is sufficient to establish the duty to respond; subjective certainty is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator monitoring for and addressing barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(b): recipients must require their Title IX Coordinators to monitor for and address barriers in their education programs or activities that would prevent or deter individuals from reporting possible sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barriers include inaccessible reporting processes, unfamiliarity with the Coordinator or procedures, prior inadequate responses, discouraging staff, long response times, and fear of retaliation. Once aware of a barrier, recipients must take steps reasonably calculated to address it. Examples include targeted trainings, office visibility changes, publication of contact information, increased staff, enhanced training for Title IX staff, and user-friendly materials. The Department declined to mandate particular tools (e.g., climate surveys) but permits their use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor responses to identified barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient becomes aware of a barrier to reporting sex discrimination, the recipient must take steps that are reasonably calculated to address that specific barrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should be tailored to the unique factors of the educational environment. Possible responses: trainings for specific departments or staff, widespread staff/student training, enhanced Title IX office resources, relocation of the Coordinator's office for visibility, and improved materials. The Department declined to require mandated follow-up with reporters as a universal step but recognizes it may be appropriate in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of §106.44(b) — barriers to reporting (not general monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(b) is focused on barriers to reporting and does not require monitoring related to sex discrimination more generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, an online reporting system that is inaccessible to those wishing to report would constitute a barrier. Recipients should monitor for impediments that prevent or deter reporting, not be required to engage in broader monitoring of all sex discrimination absent other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient duties arise before Title IX Coordinator knowledge — training and prevention obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some duties under §106.44 arise even before the Title IX Coordinator has knowledge of particular conduct: recipients must require non-confidential employees to comply with notification requirements and confidential employees to comply with §106.44(d) through training or other measures, and must require the Title IX Coordinator to monitor for and address barriers under §106.44(b) regardless of whether the Coordinator has received information about possible sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes proactive institutional obligations (e.g., training, procedures, staffing) to ensure employees know and perform their notification and response duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal safeguards and protections for students with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(h) requires a recipient to undertake an individualized safety and risk analysis to determine whether an imminent and serious threat to health or safety arising from allegations of sex discrimination justifies removal; the respondent must be provided notice and an opportunity to challenge immediately after removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in §106.44 authorizes measures that conflict with Section 504, the IDEA, or the ADA; the emergency removal provision must not be construed to modify rights under those laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality and impartiality of Title IX Coordinator's role preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not eliminate neutrality or impartiality from the Title IX Coordinator role or require Coordinators to 'seek out' discrimination and initiate a set number of cases; the recipient is not acting as prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedure provisions, training requirements, and other regulatory protections (e.g., §§106.8(d)(2)(iii),(d)(3); 106.44(k)(4); 106.45(b)(2); 106.46(i)(iii)) are intended to ensure fairness, prevent bias, and preserve impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-enrollment and multi-recipient situations — separate obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: In dual-enrollment circumstances (e.g., a high school student taking college classes), each recipient has its own obligations under Title IX and neither should assume the other is solely responsible for responding to a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive and remedial measures may implicate both institutions; recipients should coordinate as appropriate but both retain responsibility to protect participants in their own programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative enforcement distinct from private damages standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's administrative enforcement standard under §106.44 is not required to mirror the Gebser/Davis private damages deliberate indifference framework; administrative obligations can be more robust and different in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department has authority under the Spending Clause to define recipients' regulatory obligations, provide notice when funds are accepted, and enforce compliance administratively (e.g., notice of noncompliance, opportunity to resolve before enforcement). The Department removed the deliberate indifference standard and expanded the knowledge standard to improve administrative enforcement effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to adopt Title VII standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Department sought closer alignment in some respects, Title VII employer liability standards do not bind Title IX implementation; differences in workplace and educational environments justify different administrative enforcement standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(b)-(k) are designed to impose reasonable demands needed to effectuate Title IX without necessarily adopting Title VII's negligence/constructive notice approach.
